test_title: SSC GD Constable (2022) Official Paper (Held On : 25 Jan 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in simple past tense.**

A. Last year, I have travelled to Japan.

B. Last year, I was travelling to Japan.

C. Last year, I travelled to Japan.

D. Last year, I had been travelling to Japan.
solution:
The correct answer is: **C**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence "**C. Last year, I travelled to Japan**" expresses the simple past tense.
 
• It uses the simple past tense ("**travelled**") to express a completed action in the past.
 
• It accurately conveys that the speaker traveled to Japan last year.
 
 
• **Structure of the simple past tense**: Subject + Past Simple Verb + Object__
 
• **Example**: *She visited Paris last summer.*
 
 

Thus, **option 3** is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sentence A**: This sentence contains a tense inconsistency. "Last year" already establishes a past time frame, so the past simple tense should be used.
 
• **Sentence B**: This option uses the past continuous tense ("was travelling"), which implies ongoing or continuous action in the past.
 
 
• **Structure**: Subject + Past Simple of "to be" (was/were) + Present Participle Verb (-ing form)__
 
• **Example**: *I was studying when the phone rang.*
 
 
 
• **Sentence D**: This option uses the past perfect continuous tense ("had been travelling"), indicating a continuous action that was completed before another past event.
 __
 
• **Structure**: Subject + Past Perfect of "to be" (had been) + Present Participle Verb (-ing form)__
 
• **Example**: *She had been working on the project for hours before they arrived.*
